companies.name: Metromile
companies.description: Metromile is a pay-per-mile auto insurance platform powered by telematics and data science. Customers attach the Pulse OBD device to their vehicle to track mileage; premiums consist of a base monthly rate plus a per-mile charge, rewarding low-mileage drivers with significant savings. Beyond consumer insurance, Metromile Enterprise offers a cloud-based REST API platform for property and casualty insurers covering touchless claims automation, accident reconstruction (Replay), fraud detection (Detect), digital FNOL reporting (Report), and back-office workflow automation (Streamline). Metromile was acquired by Lemonade in July 2022.

companies.name: Double Robotics
companies.description: Double Robotics builds telepresence robots for hybrid work and education, best known for the self-driving Double 3 videoconferencing robot and the earlier iPad-based Double 2. Its developer program spans three surfaces: the Double 3 SDK (a local command-and-event API exposed over a Unix domain socket on the robot, covering base movement, navigation, PTZ cameras, depth sensors, WebRTC calling, and standby/sidebar apps), iOS SDKs for the Double 2 (Basic Control and Camera Kit), and a Fleet REST API for programmatic access to fleet-management data such as robots, users, call logs, and visitor passes. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched against the company's public developer surface.

companies.name: Meshcrafts
companies.description: Meshcrafts, operating publicly as CURRENT (Current Eco AS, formerly Meshcrafts AS, of Oslo, Norway), is a charge point management system (CPMS) provider for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. Its cloud platform lets location owners and charge point operators manage EV charging points, handle payment and invoicing, apply smart energy management and load balancing, and offer white-label charging experiences to drivers. The platform is hardware-agnostic and OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) certified for OCPP 1.6 and OCPP 2.0.1, including Advanced Security, and advertises 99% uptime. Current was the first in the Nordics to reach OCPP 2.0.1 CORE and Advanced Security. The company is backed by 500 Global and surfaced in the API Evangelist network through that portfolio.

companies.name: Wingstop
companies.description: Wingstop Inc. (NASDAQ: WING) is a US-based quick-service restaurant chain specializing in cooked-to-order chicken wings, tenders, and sides across thousands of franchised and company-owned locations. Wingstop is digital-first - digital transactions account for the large majority of systemwide sales - built on its proprietary MyWingstop ordering platform and the Club Wingstop loyalty program, with consumer ordering via wingstop.com, native iOS and Android apps, and third-party delivery marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub). Wingstop does not operate a public developer program or publish open API documentation. There is no developer.wingstop.com (the host does not resolve), and ordering, loyalty, menu, and POS integrations flow through bilateral corporate and franchisee technology programs rather than open developer endpoints.

companies.name: Distribusion
companies.description: Distribusion is a Berlin-based ground transportation technology company that operates a global distribution system (GDS) for ground travel. Its B2B platform connects 2,000+ carriers - buses, trains, trams, and ferries - with 250+ retailers and travel platforms including Google Maps, Expedia, Booking, and Trainline. The Distribusion Retailer API handles the full transaction lifecycle from search to settlement: inventory search, booking, payment, unified invoicing, channel management, real-time disruption management, and after-sales services. The platform supports the OSDM (Open Sales and Distribution Model) rail distribution standard and aims to make ground travel as accessible and bookable as flights. Backed by Creandum and Northzone.

companies.name: Synop
companies.description: Synop is a software platform for commercial electric vehicle fleet charging and energy management, describing itself as "the operating system for commercial EV fleets." Its hardware- and software-agnostic platform integrates vehicles, chargers, and the grid across the U.S. and Europe, spanning charge management (remote charger control, real-time alerts, EVSE interoperability across 100+ charging station models), energy management (AI-based load and time-of-use optimization, curtailment, demand response, and vehicle-to-grid events), vehicle management (state-of-charge and efficiency via telematics), payment management (billing, driver reimbursement, and transaction reporting), utility management, and SynopLink edge connectivity for site-level operations. Synop cites 500+ MWh under management across 800+ commercial depots. Its API integrations surface live time-of-use rate data and export reimbursement data to accounting and expense systems, though the developer documentation is a password-gated ReadMe admin guide rather than a public developer portal.

companies.name: Kopperfield
companies.description: Kopperfield is a software company building design and permitting tools for electrical contractors, electricians, inspectors and instructors. Founded in 2022, the company started as an EV charger installation booking service and has since become a broader contractor platform whose stated mission is to "accelerate home electrification by giving contractors the tools they need to work faster, smarter, and with total confidence." The web and mobile product covers NEC-compliant residential and commercial load calculations, drag-and-drop single line diagrams, panel schedules with circuit directories, AI panel-photo analysis, and a National Electrical Code chatbot trained on the 2017, 2020 and 2023 code editions. Kopperfield publishes a public llms.txt and a public status page but does not currently operate a public developer program: there is no published API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal, and robots.txt disallows crawling of /api/. The company is backed by General Catalyst, MCJ Collective, Lachy Groom and Designer Fund.

companies.name: Nirvana Tech
companies.description: Nirvana Insurance (Nirvana Tech, Inc.) is a technology-driven commercial trucking insurance provider that pairs A-rated fleet insurance coverage with an AI-powered active safety platform. Nirvana ingests telematics and connected-vehicle data from motor carriers to price risk more accurately, help fleets save up to 20% on premiums, and reduce accidents through real-time safety alerts, driver coaching, and predictive risk scoring. The company serves fleets and independent insurance agents through a digital quoting and policy-management agent portal, and is backed by General Catalyst. Nirvana raised a Series D round to expand its data-driven insurance and safety products across the trucking industry. As of this profile Nirvana operates a marketing site plus an agent sign-in portal and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: AtoB
companies.description: AtoB is a fleet payments platform for the trucking and transportation industry, offering fuel cards, spend-management controls, driver payouts, and trip credit to fleets of every size. Its cards work across a nationwide fuel network with truck-stop discounts, granular purchase controls (fuel-only, category/MCC restrictions, per-transaction and daily limits), telematics-aware fraud prevention, and reporting that supports IFTA fuel-tax and expense compliance. AtoB also runs partner programs for factoring companies, freight brokers, and merchants, and exposes a private Partners API used by telematics and fleet-management integrations (for example Fleetio and Oxmaint) to sync cards, drivers, vehicles, and settled fuel transactions. AtoB was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and General Catalyst; this profile has been enriched from public web sources.

companies.name: Rhythmos
companies.description: Rhythmos (rhythmos.io) provides modern analytics for managing electric-vehicle charging and grid infrastructure. Its platform coordinates fleet charging needs against utility and wholesale market conditions to lower energy costs and defer costly grid infrastructure investment, serving EV fleet owners, utilities, municipalities, and market aggregators through Fleet, Grid, and Market applications. Rhythmos maintains a SOC 2 Type II report and is GDPR compliant. The company is now part of Electron (electron.net). No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, website properties, and security/compliance posture.

companies.name: Root Insurance
companies.description: Root is a U.S. app-first auto insurer that prices policies primarily on real driving behavior captured by smartphone telematics. The Root mobile app handles enrollment, telematics scoring, policy management, claims, and optional roadside assistance, with renters insurance as an add-on line. Root has reorganized its tech stack around APIs to power embedded auto insurance with partners such as Carvana and Hyundai Capital America; partner APIs are gated and not publicly documented. Note: Root Insurance (joinroot.com) is distinct from the unrelated Root Platform (rootplatform.com) insurtech in South Africa / UK.

companies.name: Metropolis Technologies
companies.description: Metropolis Technologies is an AI-powered recognition platform that uses computer vision to make real-world physical spaces responsive, best known as the largest U.S. parking operator with checkout-free parking across 4,200+ North American locations. Founded in 2017, the company powers what it calls the "Recognition Economy" — vehicles are recognized on entry and exit so members pay automatically without tickets, gates, or lines. Metropolis scaled through the acquisitions of Premier Parking (2022) and SP Plus Corporation (2024), raised $1.6 billion in financing in 2025, and was named a TIME100 Most Influential Company of 2026. It provides access to your data in a way that works best for you, whether through integration, automation, or full customization. The API is RESTful with JSON responses, and Android and iOS SDKs are available on request.

companies.name: Platform Science
companies.description: Platform Science is an enterprise connected-vehicle and fleet management platform for commercial trucking and transportation. It combines ELD and telematics, driver applications (Hours of Service, DVIR, navigation, workflow, media management), back-office fleet management, and video safety intelligence on a single connected-vehicle platform. Its Virtual Vehicle Marketplace hosts 100+ partner integrations across 18 categories (asset tracking, compliance, fuel, navigation, sensors, TMS, and more), and a gated developer program (the Remote Platform Management system, an Android SDK, and a data-retrieval API governed by SPEED Certification) lets partners build edge and cloud integrations against the platform.

companies.name: Didi
companies.description: DiDi Global is a mobility technology platform best known for ride-hailing, taxi-hailing, and enterprise employee travel across China and international markets. DiDi exposes a public developer surface through DiDi Enterprise Services (DDES) — an Open API for corporate travel management covering approval workflows, bills, budget/cost centers, orders, single sign-on, users, roles, and company entities. The DDES API (base URL https://api.es.xiaojukeji.com) is documented at opendocs.xiaojukeji.com/version2024, secured with OAuth 2.0 client_credentials plus per-request signing, and shipped with official Java and Go SDKs under the github.com/didi organization. DiDi is backed by Hillhouse and the SoftBank Vision Fund.

companies.name: ChowNow
companies.description: ChowNow is a Playa Vista, Los Angeles-based restaurant technology company providing commission-free online ordering, branded mobile apps, marketing tools, and operational software purpose-built for independent restaurants. Founded in 2011, ChowNow powers ordering websites, native iOS/Android apps, QR-code dine-in ordering, catering, email and SMS marketing, a rewards program, Flex Delivery, order aggregation, and centralized menu management for 20,000+ restaurants. The platform integrates with 20+ point-of-sale systems including Toast, Square, Revel, Clover, Lightspeed, Heartland Genius, Skytab, and PosiTouch, and syndicates restaurant menus through a Discovery Network spanning Google, Apple Maps, Yelp, and other channels, with optional hand-off to DoorDash, UberEats, and Grubhub for last-mile delivery. ChowNow's business model is flat-fee software-as-a-service for restaurants rather than per-order commissions, and the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks reference, or open developer portal. Third-party integration is handled through pre-built connectors managed inside the restaurant dashboard and a private partnerships program; prospective POS, delivery, and technology partners apply through a partnerships form rather than self-serve API documentation. The company's public GitHub presence consists primarily of forks of open-source Python/JavaScript tooling and archived internal libraries, with no SDK, client library, or specification repositories.

companies.name: Ambi Robotics
companies.description: Ambi Robotics is a Berkeley, California AI robotics company building parcel-sortation and induction robots for ecommerce, postal, and logistics workflows. Founded in 2018 as Ambidextrous Laboratories — a spin-out of UC Berkeley's Dex-Net Project led by Ken Goldberg — by Jeff Mahler (CTO), Stephen McKinley, David Gealy, and Matt Matl, with Jim Liefer (ex-Walmart, ex-UPS) as CEO. Its flagship products are AmbiSort A-Series (sort-to-sack small parcel sorting), AmbiSort B-Series (sort-to-gaylord parcel induction for middle-mile and reverse logistics), AmbiStack (mixed-case stacking for inbound and outbound), and AmbiVision (3D dimensioning, OCR, defect detection, and visual quality inspection). All robots run AmbiOS, the company's cloud-native "operating system for physical intelligence," comprising the AI Skill Suite (Sort, Stack, Kit, Pack, Induct apps), the PRIME-1 foundation model trained on millions of real-world operations, AmbiVision perception, AmbiAccess fleet management dashboard with heat maps and remote support, and a Sim2Real training pipeline that compresses model training by up to 10,000x. Ambi Robotics' primary commercial deployment is a $23 million expansion with Pitney Bowes, with AmbiSort A-Series and B-Series systems deployed across Pitney Bowes ecommerce hubs in the US (including the Stockton, CA hub that nearly doubled local-direct-delivery throughput in the 2021 peak holiday season, and middle-mile B-Series systems that sorted more than 3 million parcels within four months of deployment). Ambi Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for AmbiOS, AmbiSort, AmbiStack, or PRIME-1; integration with customer WMS/WES systems is performed by Ambi's solutions team. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (Ray, trimesh, FCL, EIPScanner, tinygltf, rapier, jszmq, CVXPYgen, mongoose-delete) and internal CI/CD workflow utilities — no published API spec, SDK package, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Progressive Insurance
companies.description: One of the largest auto insurance providers in the United States offering personal auto, motorcycle, boat, RV, home, renters, and commercial insurance. Progressive is known for its direct-to-consumer model (1-800-PROGRESSIVE and progressive.com), its independent-agent channel, the comparative rate quoting experience, and the Snapshot usage-based insurance program that prices premiums against telematics-captured driving behaviour from a plug-in OBD-II dongle or the Snapshot mobile app. Progressive also runs the ForAgents agent portal and a public Developer Portal at developer.progressive.com that hosts embedded-quoting APIs for partners — including the Embedded Direct auto quoting API, the Commercial Auto Quoting product, and the Certificate of Insurance API — alongside private B2B integrations with comparative-rater carriers, agency-management systems, and telematics providers.

companies.name: Urtopia

companies.name: FordPass / Ford Pro
companies.description: FordPass is Ford Motor Company's consumer connected-vehicle mobile app and service platform for Ford and Lincoln owners, exposing remote start/stop, remote lock/unlock, vehicle status (fuel/charge, tire pressure, oil life, odometer, location), Vehicle Health alerts, BlueCruise hands-free driving, Wi-Fi hotspot, Phone As A Key, scheduled service, and roadside assistance via the embedded FordPass Connect 4G LTE modem. Ford Pro Telematics is integrated with Geotab, Fleetio, Samsara, Motive, Verizon Connect, and other fleet platforms, and Smartcar offers a consumer OAuth bridge to Ford vehicles using FordPass Connect credentials. Access to Ford APIs is gated behind a partner application and credentials issued through the Ford Developer Portal; Ford has periodically restricted individual-developer access. No public OpenAPI specification is published outside the partner portal, so this profile documents the Ford developer surface as an index without a generated machine-readable contract.

companies.name: Poplin
companies.description: Poplin (formerly SudShare) is a nationwide on-demand laundry pickup and delivery marketplace connecting customers with independent, work-from-home "Laundry Pros" who wash, dry, and fold laundry, serving 500+ cities and 150,000+ customers. Poplin operates two consumer-facing mobile apps - the customer app and the Laundry Pro app - plus a Laundry Pro web portal (laundry-pro.poplin.co), but it does not expose a public or partner developer API. No developer portal or API reference was found at poplin.co, and the api.poplin.co subdomain resolves but returns a bare 404 with no documentation, indicating internal-only use. Business/SMB accounts (property managers, hospitality) are onboarded through sales and an account manager rather than through self-service API keys.

companies.name: Rappi
companies.description: Rappi is a Colombian-founded pan-Latin American super-app headquartered in Bogotá, with regional hubs in São Paulo and Mexico City. Founded in 2015 by Simón Borrero, Sebastián Mejía, and Felipe Villamarín, and accelerated through Y Combinator's W16 batch, Rappi operates across Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, and Uruguay. The platform bundles on-demand delivery (restaurants, groceries via "Súper" and Turbo Fresh, pharmacies, retail, alcohol) with consumer fintech (RappiPay, RappiCard, RappiCash) and adjacent services such as RappiTravel and the RappiPrime subscription. Rappi's developer surface is operated through its Partners program at dev-portal.rappi.com, where approved restaurants, retailers, and middleware providers obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials to integrate with a REST API for menu and catalog management, store availability, order lifecycle events, financial reconciliation, and webhook subscriptions. companies.name: Getaround
companies.description: Getaround is a peer-to-peer car-sharing marketplace and connected-car technology company founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, with significant European operations across France, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Norway, and the United Kingdom. The platform pairs private and professional vehicle owners with renters who book cars by the hour or day, unlocking and starting vehicles from a mobile app rather than meeting the owner to exchange keys. The keyless experience is enabled by Getaround Connect, a proprietary in-car telematics device that the company designs and installs in shared vehicles to handle remote lock/unlock, ignition, GPS tracking, mileage reporting, fuel level monitoring, and trip event recording. Getaround acquired Drivy in 2019 to consolidate the European car-sharing market and acquired the HyreCar rideshare-driver rental marketplace in 2022. The company went public on the NYSE via a SPAC merger in December 2022 at a valuation of roughly $1.2 billion, was delisted from the NYSE in July 2024 and transferred to OTC Pink under the ticker GETR after its market capitalization collapsed to roughly $24 million. On February 11, 2025, Getaround announced it was ceasing all United States operations — including HyreCar — while preserving its European business, which continues to operate in major EU cities under the same Getaround Connect platform. Getaround has never published a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; partner integrations with insurers, fleet operators, and automotive OEMs have historically been delivered through private, contract-bound APIs rather than a self-service developer surface. The company's GitHub organization hosts primarily forks of generic open-source libraries (Braintree SDKs, iOS testing frameworks, logging libraries) rather than first-party API artifacts.

Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden and publicly listed on Nasdaq (ticker PSNY) since 2022, Polestar designs and sells a lineup of battery-electric vehicles — Polestar 1 (discontinued hybrid GT), Polestar 2 (fastback), Polestar 3 (SUV manufactured in South Carolina and Chengdu), Polestar 4 (SUV coupe), and the upcoming Polestar 5 GT. The vehicles run a Google Automotive Services–based infotainment platform with Google built-in (Maps, Assistant, Play Store), and support NACS-compatible DC fast charging in North America. Polestar emphasizes sustainability through the Polestar 0 project (climate-neutral car by 2030) and partnerships with Circulor for battery traceability. Polestar does not currently publish or document a public developer API, SDK, OEM connected-car API, or partner integration programme; all known third-party Polestar integrations (Home Assistant, community Python clients) rely on reverse-engineering the unauthenticated customer app endpoints and are explicitly unsupported by Polestar.

companies.name: Yassir
companies.description: Yassir is an Algerian-founded super app providing on-demand and financial services across the Maghreb, sub-Saharan Africa, Canada, and France. Founded in 2017 by Noureddine Tayebi and headquartered in Palo Alto, California with operations centered in Algiers, the company bundles ride-hailing (Yassir Ride), food delivery (Yassir Food), grocery delivery (Yassir Market), and digital financial services (Yassir Cash) into a single consumer mobile app, alongside a Yassir B2B suite covering corporate mobility, meal benefits, procurement, parcel delivery, and digital gift cards. Yassir reports more than six million users, 130,000+ driver and merchant partners, and 4,500 employees operating across cities in Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, South Africa, Senegal, Canada, and France. The company has raised roughly $193M to date, including a $150M Series B led by BOND with participation from Y Combinator and DN Capital, and a global sponsorship partnership with Paris Saint-Germain. Yassir is a consumer and merchant-facing super app: it operates iOS and Android apps and a business portal (go-business.yassir.com) but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source project. Driver, courier, restaurant, and store onboarding flow through partner sign-up forms rather than a developer program, and the yassir-tech GitHub organization currently has no public repositories.

companies.name: Dada
companies.description: Dada Group (Dada Nexus, NASDAQ: DADA) is a leading Chinese instant retail and local on-demand delivery platform, headquartered in Shanghai and founded in 2014. It operates an open, crowdsourced delivery network of more than one million rider partners serving supermarkets, pharmacies, fresh-food and restaurant merchants across thousands of counties and cities, alongside merchant fulfillment products such as the Haibo in-store logistics system and the Dada Youjian picking service. Now integrated into the JD.com ecosystem, its core delivery brand was rebranded to JD Instant Delivery (京东秒送) in May 2024. Dada runs a merchant Open Platform (开放平台) for order, delivery-tracking and fulfillment integrations. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Flock
companies.description: Flock is a London-based commercial motor and fleet insurtech that provides usage-based, data-driven insurance for businesses operating vehicle fleets. Using real-time telematics and data science, Flock prices risk dynamically and rewards safer driving with lower premiums, delivering connected fleet insurance through a digital platform and partner integrations. The company is backed by Anthemis and other investors and operates primarily in the United Kingdom. This API Evangelist profile tracks Flock's public developer and company surface; as of this enrichment pass Flock publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

companies.name: IKEA U.S.
companies.description: IKEA U.S. is the United States retail operation of IKEA, run by Ingka Group, the largest IKEA franchisee. The U.S. business operates ~50+ full-service stores, ~40+ Plan & Order Points, and ~80+ pick-up locations across the country, alongside the ikea.com/us e-commerce site and the IKEA mobile app. Inter IKEA Systems B.V. separately owns the IKEA Concept and brand. IKEA U.S. offers home furnishings, kitchens, appliances, lighting, the IKEA Family loyalty program, the IKEA Business Network for B2B customers, home delivery and Click & Collect, design and planning services, the Buy Back & Resell program, and IKEA Home smart products controlled via the IKEA Home smart and IKEA Home smart 1 apps. IKEA U.S. does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading-partner integrations are handled through IKEA's vendor systems and Ingka Group's internal digital platforms.

companies.name: Alba Robot
companies.description: ALBA Robot is a Turin, Italy based autonomous micro-mobility company building a fleet of self-driving robots for indoor and pedestrian spaces such as airports, hospitals, and large facilities. Its product line includes ALBA One, ALBA Ride, ALBA Ride +, and the ALBA Caddie autonomous baggage transport robot, and it layers digital services such as Digital Twins and Digital Out-of-Home (DOOH) advertising on top of the mobility platform. ALBA Robot runs pilots and deployments with airports including Cagliari, London Gatwick, Dallas, Milan, Turin, and Dubai (with dnata), and operates from Turin with a US presence in Detroit, Michigan. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Floward is backed by investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks Floward as a company in the network; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and corporate site but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found.

companies.name: GoTo
companies.description: GoTo (PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, IDX: GOTO) is the largest technology group in Indonesia, formed in May 2021 through the merger of the on-demand and ride-hailing pioneer Gojek and the e-commerce marketplace Tokopedia. GoTo operates a super-app ecosystem spanning on-demand services (ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery, logistics), e-commerce, and financial technology through GoTo Financial (including GoPay, one of Indonesia's leading digital wallets). Its business-intelligence layer applies predictive analytics for tire wear and route optimization, and it integrates with major telematics providers such as Samsara, Geotab, Netfleet, and Traffilog plus ERP systems via direct API connections. Ruedata is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or developer portal.

companies.name: Tibo Energy
companies.description: Tibo Energy is an Eindhoven-based energy software company building an AI-driven Energy Management System (EMS) for commercial and industrial customers. Its SaaS platform simulates, monitors, and autonomously controls on-site energy hubs and smart grids, coordinating distributed assets such as heat pumps, EV charging stations, and battery storage to cut energy costs and emissions and to unlock additional capacity from existing infrastructure without waiting for grid upgrades. Tibo connects hardware through standard protocols such as MODBUS and OCPP via the Tibo Gateway and exchanges data with BMS, SCADA, and ERP systems through open APIs. Since launching in late 2023 it has deployed its EMS across more than 30 industrial sites and is backed by KOMPAS VC, Hitachi Ventures, SET Ventures, WEPA Ventures, and Speedinvest.

companies.name: Tractable
companies.description: Tractable is a London-headquartered artificial intelligence company founded in 2014 by Alexandre Dalyac, Razvan Ranca, and Adrien Cohen that applies computer vision and deep learning to automate visual damage assessment for auto and property insurance claims. The platform analyzes photos of vehicles and buildings down to the pixel to produce accident first-notice- of-loss (FNOL) triage decisions, AI-generated preliminary repair estimates, automated claim review for fraud and consistency, subrogation packet analysis, and property repair-cost estimation and underwriting condition assessment. Tractable's flagship offerings include Auto Estimator, Auto Damage Appraiser, Auto Salvage, Property Estimator, Property Underwriter, and the LumaScanner fixed-operations vehicle scanning product. The company serves insurers, dealerships, repair networks, recyclers, and fleet and rental operators including GEICO, Aviva, Mitchell, Tokio Marine, Admiral, Sompo, Aioi Nissay Dowa, and LKQ. Tractable reached unicorn status in June 2021 and secured a $65M investment from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 in July 2023, scaling to over 300 employees across offices in London, Warsaw, Paris, Milan, Spain, Romania, New York, Toronto, Tokyo, and Bangkok. The product is delivered through flexible desktop and API integrations with FNOL, estimatics, and claim review systems, but the developer surface is gated to enterprise partners — there is no public developer portal, self-service API key, OpenAPI specification, SDK release, or open-source repository, and no publicly published authentication, endpoint, pricing, or rate-limit documentation.

There is no current public OpenAPI specification, self-serve API key, or open-access developer documentation for Citymapper.

companies.name: RoboDock
companies.description: RoboDock is an autonomous robotics company (Y Combinator W2026) building the robotics layer that powers autonomous EV and AV depots, starting with charging and inspections. companies.name: Automatic
companies.description: Automatic (Automatic Labs, Inc.) was a San Francisco connected-car company founded in 2011 by Thejo Kote and Jerry Jariyasunant. Its OBD-II adapter and companion mobile app turned almost any car built since 1996 into a connected car, adding trip logging, fuel and MPG tracking, engine-light diagnostics, parking recall, and automatic crash alerts. Automatic ran a public developer platform at developer.automatic.com built around three surfaces: a REST API exposing trip, user, and vehicle data; an Events API delivering real-time driving events such as ignition on/off, hard braking, acceleration, speeding, and location changes over webhooks and websockets; and a private-beta Streaming SDK that read raw OBD-II data from the second-generation adapter over Bluetooth. SiriusXM acquired the company on 2017-04-27 for approximately $115 million, and all operations were shut down on 2020-05-28. THIS COMPANY IS DEFUNCT — no API, developer portal, or documentation remains online, and the automatic.com domain now belongs to the unrelated company Automattic. This profile is retained as a historical record of a notable connected-car API platform.

companies.name: Bidgely
companies.description: Bidgely is a Mountain View, California energy analytics company that builds AI software for electric and gas utilities. Its flagship platform, UtilityAI, applies patented non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) and disaggregation techniques to smart meter interval data to infer appliance-level energy usage — air conditioning, heat pumps, electric vehicles, pool pumps, water heaters and more — from the whole-home meter signal alone, without surveys, sub-meters, or smart plugs. The platform layers GenAI natural-language interfaces and Agentic AI workflows on top of disaggregation to support utility programs across demand-side management, customer engagement and high-bill alerts, load flexibility and time-of-use, electrification (EV and heat pump targeting), grid resiliency and DER planning, affordability and income-qualified outreach, gas efficiency, small and mid-sized business programs, and energy theft detection. Bidgely is sold to utilities as SaaS or deployable into customer AWS, Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, and Oracle environments, and exposes embeddable customer-facing widgets to utility digital channels. Bidgely has been deployed by more than 50 utilities across four continents — including FortisBC, Arizona Public Service, PacifiCorp, Avista, NV Energy, Nova Scotia Power, and SoCalGas — covering tens of millions of meters. Bidgely operates an internal REST API surface across regional endpoints (naapi.bidgely.com, api.eu.bidgely.com) for its own pilot deployments and embeddable widgets, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API key program; integration is conducted under utility contracts.

companies.name: Enel X
companies.description: Enel X is the advanced-energy-services business line of the Enel Group, an Italian multinational utility headquartered in Rome. Enel X delivers smart energy products and services across electrification, e-mobility, demand response, virtual power plants, and distributed energy resource (DER) management for residential, commercial, industrial, public-sector, and utility customers. Its principal offerings include the Enel X Way app and network for electric-vehicle charging (the consolidated successor to JuicePass and JuiceNet), the JuiceBox and JuicePedestal hardware lines, the JuiceNet Utility Edition managed-charging platform, the DER.OS / DER optimization software (now run as Calibrant Energy in North America after Enel's 2023 divestiture of its North American demand-response business), Enel X Flex flexibility management software, and VPP Connect, a set of API endpoints that lets third-party DER operators — OEMs, automation providers, and equipment manufacturers — aggregate EV chargers, batteries, HVAC systems, heat pumps, and other controllable assets into Enel's virtual power plant and earn revenue from demand-response and grid-services programs via either the open Automated Demand Response (oADR) protocol or a custom Enel API. Enel X exposes additional non-public surfaces — including the emobility.enelx.com OAuth/charging endpoints used by the Enel X Way mobile apps — but does not publish OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal; VPP Connect documentation is delivered under partnership agreement after a guided onboarding process. The official Enelx GitHub organization has effectively no public engineering presence, and the legacy JuiceNet public API has been deprecated as part of the platform migration to Enel X Way.

companies.name: GM OnStar
companies.description: GM OnStar is General Motors' connected vehicle services platform, originally launched in 1996 as an in-vehicle safety, security, and concierge service and since extended into a commercial data platform under OnStar Business Solutions. The OnStar Business Solutions API and Data Services product delivers near-real-time embedded telematics straight from properly equipped 2015-model-year-or-newer GM vehicles — Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac — without aftermarket hardware, exposing vehicle location, speed, ignition status, odometer, fuel level, EV state-of-charge and charging status, tire pressure, seatbelt status, diagnostic trouble codes, and driver-behavior events such as hard brake and hard acceleration. The product is packaged into tiered plans (commonly referenced as API Starter and API Pro) and is distributed primarily through OnStar's enterprise channel under the GM Envolve commercial brand, plus integrations with fleet management providers including Samsara, Geotab, Wheels, Verizon Connect, and other approved telematic service providers. There is no public self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI specification — access is gated through GM/OnStar sales (developer.gm.com is a request-access endpoint) or via an authorized integration partner. Consumer-facing OnStar mobile features (remote start, remote lock, vehicle locate, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, Super Cruise telemetry) are delivered through GM's myChevrolet, myBuick, myGMC, and myCadillac apps and are not part of the published API surface.

Kobo360 serves large FMCG, manufacturing, and commodities customers including Dangote, DHL, Honeywell, Olam, and Unilever, and has raised funding from investors such as Goldman Sachs, IFC, TLcom Capital, and Western Asset. Founded in 2016 by Josh Sandler, Jean-Claude Homawoo, and Ernest Gichini Ngaruiya, the company is now led by CEO Uche Ogboi and runs operations from offices in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda, moving cargo across roughly 12 African countries with a network of 20,000+ trucks and over $10B of cargo facilitated. The platform offers shippers instant rate estimates, load matching, real-time shipment tracking, electronic proof of delivery, and integrated payments, while giving transporters access to cargo orders, truck-availability management, and prompt payment on delivery. Lori operates a public rate-card tool at ratecard.lorisystems.com, but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification; its GitHub organization is limited to small internal-tooling repositories (a Singer.io tap for Freshsales, a BambooHR Python client, a Kubernetes Terraform provider, and similar utilities) rather than a customer-facing API surface.

A 500 Startups (500 Global) Batch 25 company, Nanogrid raised roughly $150K from 500 Global and Plug and Play Tech Center before being acquired by clean-energy company Arcadia on April 22, 2021. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. companies.description: Rubicon (formerly NYSE: RBT) is a waste, recycling, and sustainability technology company founded in 2008. It went public in 2022 via a SPAC merger with Founder SPAC at a pro forma valuation of roughly $1.7 billion, branding itself a "digital challenger" to the traditional waste-hauling industry with a marketplace connecting waste generators to independent haulers plus the RUBICONSmartCity fleet-and-routing platform used by more than 70 municipalities. Operating Status: the company subsequently faced severe financial distress - layoffs and debt restructuring in 2023, a June 2024 NYSE delisting, and a May 2024 divestiture of its entire fleet technology and smart-city business unit (RUBICONSmartCity, RUBICONPro, RUBICONPremier) to Rodina Capital for roughly $68 million plus a possible $12 million earnout; those assets were subsequently absorbed by Routeware. In early 2025 Rubicon deregistered its securities and became a privately held company, majority-owned by Jose Miguel Enrich through MBI Holdings, and remains the subject of shareholder litigation over the change-of-control terms. The surviving company operates as a smaller enterprise waste brokerage and sustainability-data business built around the RUBICONConnect platform (service, equipment, pickup, and cost visibility for enterprise customers such as Chipotle and FedEx), alongside RUBICONRegWatch compliance tooling, sustainability reporting, technical advisory services, and the Rubicon Now on-demand dumpster-rental service in a handful of cities. rubicon.com publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no OpenAPI specification. The only discoverable API artifact tied to the rubicon.com domain is a "Routeware Smartcity Public Api" Swagger UI hosted at a dev subdomain (haulerpublic-api.dev.aws.rubicon.com) - leftover infrastructure from the divested fleet/smart-city business - which returned a 503 Service Unavailable on every check during this review and is not publicly documented or reachable. Any hauler or municipal system integration Rubicon references (for example, connecting to city 311 systems) is negotiated per partner and gated behind sales and onboarding rather than exposed through self-serve developer documentation. Pricing across RUBICONConnect and Rubicon's enterprise services is entirely quote-based and negotiated per contract; no public pricing, tiers, or rate limits are published. This entry is maintained as an honest stub pending any future public API surface.

companies.description: Energy and Utilities is a topic profile in the API Evangelist Network cataloging the API surfaces that move data across the modern electricity, gas, and water value chain. It indexes utility data integration APIs, grid and wholesale market operator APIs, federal energy data programs, renewable energy research APIs, weather APIs that drive grid demand and solar forecasting, EV charging interoperability protocols, and the Green Button family of customer energy data standards. companies.name: Open Charge Map
companies.description: Open Charge Map is the global public registry of electric vehicle charging locations, established in 2011 as a non-commercial, community-driven project. The platform maintains a crowdsourced dataset of 300,000+ charging points worldwide, combining manually entered data with imported open data from government registries and charging networks. The REST API enables developers to search and retrieve POI (Points of Interest) data on EV charging stations, including location details, equipment specifications, connection types, operator information, and user-submitted check-ins and photos. Data can be filtered by geographic coordinates, bounding box, country, operator, connection type, charging level, and operational status. The API is free to use with an API key registration and supports both read (GET) and write (POST) operations for contributing new charging location data.
